subject: AURA · Thu 26 Nov · BREAKING: CBN appoints Murtala Mohammed as acting CEO of Keystone Bank
preheader: Also: FG adopts national e-pharmacy policy to curb drug misuse, self-medication · 3 stories, 0 risk alerts

overview.text: The Central Bank of Nigeria has appointed Murtala Mohammed as Acting Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Keystone Bank Limited, replacing Hassan Imam.
The Federal Government has adopted a national e-pharmacy policy aimed at curbing drug misuse and self-medication.
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has closed its prosecution case against former minister Agunloye, who is set to file a no-case submission.

cards.headline: BREAKING: CBN appoints Murtala Mohammed as acting CEO of Keystone Bank
cards.what_happened: The Central Bank of Nigeria has appointed Murtala Mohammed as Acting Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Keystone Bank Limited, replacing Hassan Imam. The appointment takes effect from November 26, 2026. The CBN announced the change in a statement issued on Thursday.
key_facts: Murtala Mohammed appointed Acting Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Keystone Bank Limited.
Statement issued by CBN Director of Corporate Communications and Investor Relations Michael Akuka.
analysis: Why it matters: A regulator-driven change in the chief executive of a commercial bank affects leadership continuity and oversight of a financial institution in Nigeria.

cards.headline: FG adopts national e-pharmacy policy to curb drug misuse, self-medication
cards.what_happened: The Federal Government has adopted a national e-pharmacy policy aimed at curbing drug misuse and self-medication.
analysis: Why it matters: A national e-pharmacy policy sets new regulatory rules for how medicines are sold and dispensed, which may affect pharmacy operators and drug distributors.

cards.headline: Ex-Minister Agunloye set to file no-case submission as EFCC closes case
cards.what_happened: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has closed its prosecution case against former minister Agunloye, who is set to file a no-case submission. The development was reported by Premium Times Nigeria. The article text provides no further detail on the charges or the court proceedings.
key_facts: Agunloye is set to file a no-case submission.
